candidates.headline: City to continue to investigate safety improvements for Howard Street
candidates.summary:
City of Greater Bendigo Mayor Cr Thomas Prince said while the City will not proceed with the trial, it will continue to investigate, review, implement and advocate for traffic safety improvements within the Howard Street corridor and surrounding road network in partnership with government agencies and stakeholders.

A recurring theme across the consultation was support for longer-term solutions, including improved school access and parking, enhanced pedestrian infrastructure, and advocacy for a dedicated freight corridor or alternative freight route to address growing transport demands in the area.

candidates.headline: Improvements to Bendigo Library's Public Toilet and Parent Facilities completed
candidates.summary:
The City of Greater Bendigo has completed a major project to improve the Bendigo Library’s public toilet and parent facilities to comply with the current National Construction Code and make them safer and easier to access.

Demolition of the old public toilet area and construction of new self-contained toilet cubicles to improve safety and efficiency

Construction of a dedicated cleaner’s room for improved cleaning functionality

Today Member for Bendigo West Maree Edwards, Goldfields Library CEO Mark Hands and City of Greater Bendigo Healthy Communities and Environments Director Jess Howard inspected the new facilities.

candidates.headline: $2M boost to unlock next stage of GV Link Enterprise Park - The Shepparton Adviser
candidates.summary: GREATER Shepparton’s push to attract new businesses and jobs has received a $2 million boost, with the Victorian Government funding set to help progress the next stage of GV Link Enterprise Park. Greater Shepparton City Council welcomed the investment, which will fund critical infrastructure needed to prepare additional industrial lots for development and attract future business investment. Mayor Geoff Akers said the funding was a major vote of confidence in the region’s economic future, with demand for industrial land continuing to grow. Council will now progress detailed design work for Stage 2 and seek expressions of interest for the remaining lots to better understand industry demand. The expansion is expected to create opportunities for business growth, freight and logistics investment, and employment across Shepparton and the wider Goulburn Valley.

candidates.headline: A funding story - The Shepparton Adviser
candidates.summary:
The Fairley Leadership Program began in 1997 with modest funding and a belief that investing in local people could strengthen an entire region.

Government investment continued between 2020 and 2023 through the Regional Community Leadership Program Fund and Department of Jobs, Precincts and Regions.

Throughout its history, that investment has been complemented by participant scholarships, including support from organisations such as the Gardiner Foundation and Hugh Williamson Foundation.

Their contribution also demonstrates that sustaining regional leadership is not the responsibility of any one organisation or sector. It is something businesses, governments, philanthropic organisations and communities can collectively invest in, helping ensure the next generation of local leaders has the same opportunity to step forward.

candidates.headline: Library loos well worth the wait
candidates.summary:
The main entry to the library was closed from April during the construction period. Photo: Adam Carswell/file

The major upgrade of the public toilets and parent facilities at Bendigo Library has been completed in compliance with the National Construction Code.

The project was funded by a $412,586 grant from the state government’s Living Libraries Infrastructure Program and a contribution from the city.

“The new facilities have transformed the library and the city is very appreciative of the funding received from the Victorian Government to undertake this project.”

candidates.headline: JobsPositions vacant at Foodmach
candidates.summary:
Foodmach is one of Australasia's largest privately-owned and operated packaging machinery manufacturers and integrators.

Foodmach's 7,100m2 manufacturing facilities are in Echuca, Victoria, with engineering sales offices in Melbourne, Sydney, Adelaide and Brisbane.

Foodmach is an Equal Opportunity Employer that values diversity of all kinds in the workplace.Join us and be part of a winning team!

Foodmach is seeking an experienced Industrial Electrician to join our growing manufacturing team in Echuca. Working from our workshop, you will be involved in the electrical assembly, wiring, testing, fault finding and commissioning of advanced packaging, materials handling and automation systems for some of Australia's leading food, beverage and manufacturing businesses. This is an excellent opportunity for a tradesperson looking to work on complex automation projects rather than repetitive maintenance work. You'll work closely with our engineering, manufacturing and project teams to build state-of-the-art equipment that is deployed across Australia and New Zealand. Occasional travel to customer sites across Australia and overseas is required, including some time away from home.
